item.text: I’m checking the current implementation for a refactor that improves correctness or structure, not just rearranges lines. The most likely target now is the value-validation path and the repetitive test layout.

I found a real correctness gap: `NaN` and infinities currently slip past validation because the range checks alone don’t reject non-finite floats. I’m fixing that and reducing some repetition in the test harness at the same time.
The test patch didn’t apply cleanly, so I’m re-reading the current file and applying the refactor against the exact contents rather than forcing it.
I’ve got the exact file contents now. Applying the validation fix and the smaller test refactor against the current revision.

The validation path now rejects non-finite floats explicitly, and the test harness has less duplication. I’m recompiling and rerunning the demo plus tests to verify the refactor and the new rejection cases.

Refactored the validation path in [BucketSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSort.java:1) by extracting `isSupportedValue(...)` and tightening the contract to reject non-finite floats. The previous range-only check allowed `NaN` and infinities through, which was a real correctness gap.

I also cleaned up [BucketSortTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSortTest.java:1) by introducing small assertion helpers for in-place and copy-based sorting, which removes repeated setup code. The test coverage now includes `NaN`, negative values, and positive infinity in addition to the earlier boundary cases.
